01
Introduction

Reason for the Evaluation

Lucía and Sinho contacted us because of Tarzán's aggressive behavior, particularly toward unfamiliar people and other dogs. According to what they told us, he already has a history of biting six different people, and they are looking for a solution before a more serious accident occurs.

Tarzán is a large and powerful Boerboel, with an estimated weight of 60 to 80 kg. Although he is a very affectionate dog with his family, his reactions toward people outside the household can be difficult to control. Because of his size, even a brief reaction can cause significant injuries.

⚠ Euthanasia was considered

The family has also considered the possibility of euthanasia because of these incidents. However, Lucía and Sinho want to give Tarzán a chance through training, which is why we conducted this evaluation.

⚠ Our goal

Our goal is to determine Tarzán's potential for improvement, identify the main risks, and recommend a training program that can help create a safer living environment.

02
Background

Family Life and Background

His Relationship with the Family

Tarzán with a family member

Tarzán lives in a large household that includes young children and domestic staff. At home, both Tarzán and Bella are generally affectionate, playful, and close to their owners.

One particularly heartwarming observation is the relationship they have with Enrique, one of the family's children. According to what we were told, the dogs seem to understand his instructions even when his way of expressing himself verbally is difficult for other people to understand. This familiarity reflects the bond they have developed with him.

✓ A positive sign

We also observed that Tarzán seeks shelter behind his owners when he finds himself in an uncomfortable situation. We consider this a positive sign, as he appears to recognize them as people he can turn to for safety. Dr. Guzmán, who has known Tarzán since he was a puppy, is also one of the few people outside the family with whom he maintains a good relationship.

However, that trust has not yet translated into sufficiently reliable obedience when Tarzán becomes agitated. This will be one of the central aspects of his training.

Accidents Involving the Children and His Hip Injury

The owners explained that, at approximately six months of age, Tarzán was involved in an accident with a large children's ride-on toy vehicle. According to their account, he suffered a hip injury that required surgery, and one of his legs now shows a visible deformity.

Later, one of the children climbed onto the area around his lower back or hip. Tarzán reacted by attempting to bite the child, causing a small wound on the child's face. Fortunately, the injury was not more serious, but the child has been afraid of him ever since.

We consider it possible that pain associated with his injury contributed to this reaction.

⚠ Physical separation from the children

For this reason, we recommend preventing children from climbing onto the dogs or engaging in physical play that could cause them pain or discomfort. In Tarzán's case, given his history, it is currently necessary to maintain a secure physical separation between him and the children.

03
Evaluation

Evaluation Conducted During the Intake

Initial Observation

When we arrived at the property, Tarzán was inside his crate. He did not immediately begin barking at us, although the owners mentioned that he normally reacts by barking when visitors arrive.

This initial observation did not allow us to determine whether he was calm, insecure, or simply paying attention to our presence.

To begin the evaluation, we used the intermediate gate on the property as a safety barrier. The owners then placed a leash on Tarzán, and we began observing his responses in different situations.

Reactions to Being Approached

One of the first things that caught our attention was that when we attempted to approach or make contact with Tarzán, he tended to move away rather than immediately attack.

We later secured him to a tree and repeated several observations. Once again, he showed a tendency to move away. When we took the leash and attempted to guide him using simple instructions, he began showing increasingly encouraging responses.

✓ An opportunity for his training

Based on our evaluation, this represents an interesting opportunity for his training. Tarzán appears to have some ability to choose to move away when something makes him uncomfortable, although he has also learned to react aggressively in certain circumstances.

Part of our work will involve reinforcing these alternative behaviors so that he can respond without resorting to biting.

During this evaluation, we also used an aluminum chair as a protective barrier between the trainer and Tarzán. The chair was not used to strike him or provoke a reaction, but rather to maintain a safe distance while observing his behavior.

Evaluation on the Street

We then went out onto the street to observe how Tarzán reacted within his usual surroundings, particularly around other dogs.

During the walk, a dog began barking from a neighboring property, and Tarzán attempted to move toward it. When he was prevented from advancing by the leash, he reacted by jumping and attempting to bite the leash.

We interpreted this response as a possible reaction of frustration to being restrained, although other factors, such as territoriality or insecurity, could also be involved.

Fortunately, the episode ended quickly. However, this behavior deserves attention because it demonstrates that Tarzán still has difficulty accepting certain restrictions when he is agitated.

⚠ A previous incident

This also relates to a previous incident reported by the family. On that occasion, Tarzán attempted to bite someone, and his owner intervened by holding him by the neck. During the struggle, the owner accidentally applied excessive pressure, and Tarzán ended up biting his hand.

For this reason, it will be necessary to work carefully on handling Tarzán and teaching his owners safer ways to intervene in situations involving conflict.

Contact at the End of the Evaluation

At the end of the intake, we used a flat-headed mop to establish gentle physical contact with Tarzán while maintaining a safe distance.

After this contact, we observed that his behavior appeared to become more relaxed and that our presence seemed to make him less uncomfortable.

This was a favorable experience, although we still cannot guarantee that Tarzán would allow someone to approach him directly without reacting. Building that trust will require time and repeated experiences under controlled conditions.

🛈 Purpose of the evaluation

The evaluation was not a complete rehabilitation session. Its purpose was to gain a better understanding of Tarzán's reactions, his current limitations, and the possibilities for working with him.

✦ ✦ ✦
04
Assessment

Our Assessment of Tarzán's Behavior

After observing him, we believe that Tarzán has the potential to improve his behavior. We did not observe aggression as his only response in every situation.

At different moments, he preferred to move away, seek support from his owners, or accept some guidance through the leash. These responses provide a foundation on which we can begin working.

We believe his behavior may be related to a combination of factors.

Insecurity and territoriality
Lack of exposure and appropriate experiences
Difficulty accepting restrictions
Possible physical pain

Insecurity and territoriality. Tarzán appears to react particularly strongly to people and dogs entering or appearing around his environment. He may interpret certain situations as threats and respond by attempting to drive them away through aggression.

Lack of exposure and appropriate experiences. Dogs need opportunities for exploration, exercise, interaction, and adaptation to different stimuli. Insufficient exposure could contribute to Tarzán's difficulty handling unfamiliar situations.

Difficulty accepting restrictions. The reaction observed during the walk demonstrates that he still needs to improve his response when he is prevented from carrying out an action.

Possible physical pain. The owners mentioned that Tarzán spends a considerable amount of time lying down. Considering his history of hip problems, it is possible that he experiences ongoing discomfort that reduces his tolerance in certain situations.

⚠ Veterinary examination recommended

This last point deserves particular attention. We recommend a veterinary examination of his orthopedic condition and any possible pain before increasing the physical demands of training.

⚠ A cautious assessment

Although our initial observations are encouraging, the history of six people being bitten requires us to maintain a cautious assessment. It will be important to complement the training with a veterinary behavioral assessment. We cannot guarantee that the risk of biting will disappear completely.

✦ ✦ ✦
05
Safety

Escapes and Property Security

One of the main problems we identified is that Tarzán has managed to leave his designated area when certain doors have been left open.

According to the owners, on several occasions, the gardening staff have left the door to Tarzán's area open. When the main vehicle gate is subsequently opened, he finds an opportunity to escape.

Under these circumstances, Tarzán does not immediately return when called, and encounters with other people or animals can result in dangerous situations.

They also explained that he once managed to climb over a balcony barrier approximately 1 to 1.20 meters high, causing a visitor to seek refuge inside the house.

🛈 Physical limitations

This demonstrates that his physical limitations do not prevent him from overcoming certain obstacles.

Bella behind the gate

During training, we will work on territorial boundaries, waiting at doors, and responding to recall commands, with the goal of teaching Tarzán to remain within his designated areas.

However, we also recommend improving the property's physical security, particularly by installing self-closing doors, suitable locks, and a double-barrier system that prevents direct access to the main gate.

🚫 Everyone must follow the same measures

Everyone in the household, including domestic staff, must follow the same safety measures. Security cannot depend solely on someone remembering to close a door or on the dog obeying correctly.

These measures should remain in place even after training has been completed.

"Security cannot depend solely on someone remembering to close a door or on the dog obeying correctly."
Field Note · CuraDog Training
06
Training

Recommended Training Program

Complete Basic Obedience

⚠ Our initial recommendation

Our initial recommendation is to enroll Tarzán in the Complete Basic Obedience program through private training sessions, complemented by specific sessions focused on safety and handling.

This program combines the first two stages of our Basic Obedience system.

Stage 1: Simple Obedience

We focus on improving communication between the dog and his owners, establishing clear boundaries, developing self-control, and teaching owners how to handle different situations appropriately.

In Tarzán's case, this stage will be particularly useful for working on his responses to doors, people, other dogs, and restrictions during handling.

Stage 2: Commands

We will work on commands such as come, sit, stay, down, and heel, using verbal communication, hand signals, and guidance through the leash.

These skills will help develop clearer communication and a more reliable response to instructions from the family.

How We Will Organize the Training

Although the program combines the two stages described above, Tarzán's particular circumstances require us to organize the work into four progressive phases.

Phase 1. Building Trust and Introducing Basic Commands

The first sessions will focus on establishing a relationship of trust between the trainer and Tarzán, with the participation of his owners.

We will begin by working on simple commands, primarily come, sit, and stay. We will mainly use rewards and positive experiences so that Tarzán begins associating our presence with pleasant situations.

The goal is to establish safe initial communication before moving on to more demanding situations.

Phase 2. Muzzle Training and Safety Equipment

We will work on gradually introducing Tarzán to a rigid, durable, properly fitted basket-style muzzle that allows him to breathe, pant, and drink water without difficulty.

We will also teach the owners about safe handling, the proper use of control equipment, and the prevention of conflict situations, including how to respond to possible dog fights without unnecessarily exposing themselves to bites.

This part is especially important considering Tarzán's size and the previous incident in which he bit his own owner during an intervention.

Phase 3. Boundaries and Behavior Within the Property

Once we have developed the initial foundations of communication, we will begin working more extensively on the boundaries that Tarzán must respect.

We will focus particularly on controlling access to spaces, doors, distances, and restrictions established by his owners.

One of the main objectives will be teaching him not to leave the property when a door or the main gate is opened.

These skills will complement the physical security measures that must remain in place around the home.

Phase 4. Walks and Adaptation to the Surrounding Environment

Once Tarzán has developed the necessary skills and we have established appropriate safety conditions, we will begin working on walks around his home.

During this phase, we will aim to improve leash handling, his attention toward his owners, and his ability to respond more calmly to common stimuli in the neighborhood.

Once it is safe to do so and his physical condition allows it, we recommend maintaining a frequency of approximately three to seven walks per week to support continuity in his learning.

The duration and intensity of these walks must be adapted to his orthopedic problems and his response throughout the process.

Why Don't We Recommend Deep Basic from the Beginning?

This program would include everything described above, along with exposure to other environments and situations so that Tarzán can become accustomed to a wide variety of stimuli. Deep Basic Obedience is one of our most comprehensive programs because it combines the foundations of obedience with training in different locations and circumstances.

However, we do not currently consider it appropriate to begin directly with this program for Tarzán.

🛈 Foundations first

Before exposing him to environments with greater numbers of people, animals, and other stimuli, we need to establish a sufficient foundation of communication, handling, and appropriate behavior in controlled environments.

Introducing too many new situations before achieving that stability could increase the risks to Tarzán, his owners, and third parties.

For this reason, we recommend beginning with Complete Basic and considering a later exposure phase only when his progress makes it appropriate.

✦ ✦ ✦
07
Sessions

Additional Sessions and Available Time

The Complete Basic package includes ten private sessions lasting approximately 45 to 90 minutes each.

Due to Tarzán's particular needs, we anticipate additional sessions focused on muzzle training, safety equipment, and handling conflict situations. These sessions will be incorporated throughout the training process whenever most appropriate.

The number and cost of these sessions will be determined according to the needs identified.

Later, if Tarzán shows favorable progress, we can consider additional exposure sessions in different environments, including places with people, other dogs, and animals, always under appropriate safety conditions.

The family explained that Sinho generally has approximately 15 minutes per day available to dedicate to the dogs, with the possibility of increasing this to 30 minutes.

We believe that short, consistent sessions can be useful for maintaining what has been learned. We also understand that Lucía is usually at home, although her leg injury limits her mobility. Her participation can be adapted to activities she can carry out safely.

⚠ Owners' participation

The owners' participation will be essential because our goal is for the skills developed during our sessions to be maintained in the dogs' everyday lives.

08
Bella

Additional Observations About Bella

Bella

Bella, the family's other Boerboel, born on February 16, 2024, appears to have a calmer temperament than Tarzán.

⚠ Individual evaluation needed

However, the owners explained that when Tarzán attempts to attack, Bella sometimes tends to follow his lead. For this reason, we cannot assume that her behavior is completely safe without conducting an individual evaluation.

It would be advisable to assess her behavior separately before considering any specific training for her.

Reproductive Health

The owners also informed us that Bella lost eight puppies from a litter of nine, with only one surviving.

They mentioned that they suspect a possible parvovirus infection, although we do not have veterinary confirmation of the cause.

The litter was delivered by cesarean section, and Bella became pregnant again during the heat cycle following her previous pregnancy. Considering these circumstances, we recommend avoiding further breeding until a veterinarian confirms that she has recovered and is in suitable condition for another pregnancy.

🛈 Precaution

As a precautionary measure, we have suggested waiting at least one year. However, this period does not replace a medical evaluation or guarantee complete recovery.

It will also be important to assess Tarzán's orthopedic health and behavior before considering him for breeding.

Pedigree Records

The owners mentioned that both dogs come from different breeders, one of them possibly from another country.

We recommend keeping documentation of their ancestry and, in future litters, maintaining a record of their offspring and respective owners.

This record could be supported by agreements with puppy buyers to facilitate pedigree tracking, especially considering that Curaçao is a relatively small island and there could be a risk of future breeding between related dogs.

The goal would be to encourage more responsible breeding, supported by appropriate health screenings and genetic testing.

✦ ✦ ✦
09
Health

Skin Conditions and Nutrition

During the evaluation, we also identified skin abnormalities in both Tarzán and Bella, including pressure areas such as the elbows, as well as other parts of their bodies.

01 / 03Bella: skin on the ear and muzzle
02 / 03Bella: skin on the muzzle and nose
03 / 03Bella: hindquarters

Although some elbow lesions may be related to pressure from resting on hard surfaces, this does not necessarily explain the skin problems present elsewhere on their bodies.

Tarzán has a gray coat, while Bella is brown and black. Certain diluted coat colors can be associated with specific skin and coat conditions, but we cannot attribute their skin problems solely to their coloring.

⚠ Veterinary evaluation recommended

We recommend having both dogs evaluated by a veterinarian to identify the underlying causes and establish appropriate treatment.

Nutrition

Regarding nutrition, CuraDog Training has had good experiences with Taste of the Wild, particularly its salmon-based formulas, in dogs that have shown skin sensitivities. We have also received positive feedback from local veterinarians based on their own experiences.

🛈 Our recommendation, not a treatment

This recommendation is based on our experience, and we do not receive any commercial compensation from the brand. However, grain-free foods are not necessarily better for all dogs and should not be considered a general treatment for allergies. Any dietary choice should ideally be made in consultation with a veterinarian, especially when skin problems are present.

Taste of the Wild, Ancient Stream (salmon formula)

A diet based on meat and vegetables could also be considered, provided it is properly formulated to supply all the necessary nutrients. CuraDog plans to introduce this type of balanced dog food in the future, although it is not yet available as one of the company's products.

✦ ✦ ✦
10
Future

Possibility of Acquiring Another Protection Dog

During our conversation, the family also expressed an interest in possibly acquiring another large and powerful dog in the future to help protect their property.

One of the breeds discussed was the Alabai, also known as the Central Asian Shepherd Dog.

CuraDog Training knows someone in Curaçao who maintains direct contact with Alabai breeders in Russia. Through this connection, we could inquire about the possibility of obtaining a puppy, as well as the associated costs, availability, and requirements for bringing one to the island.

We have encountered exceptionally large specimens of this breed, although weights approaching 100 to 120 kg should be considered exceptional rather than typical of all Alabais.

If the family decides to acquire one in the future, we recommend beginning its education from puppyhood, including socialization, boundaries, obedience, and appropriate coexistence with the people and animals in the household.

⚠ Our priority

For now, our priority would be to improve Tarzán's safety and behavior before introducing another dog with similar characteristics.
